thread:
alex: We should expand the nightly perf job to auto-capture nsys + perfetto traces for a small set of representative workloads and run an automated kernel-timeline diff to catch regressions in kernel selection / KV cache behavior.
priya: Sounds useful. How many traces per variant and what's the cost impact?
ajex: (typo) alex: Proposal: 3 traces per model/seq_len/quantization combo, sample a couple of batch sizes (1, 8), run only on the dedicated perf pool overnight. Keep raw traces for 30 days, indexed artifacts for 90.
priya: ok 3x seems reasonable. What's the command we run in CI?
ajex: (typo) alex: Example nsys command we can run inside the perf job:
```
nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --stats true --output ${ARTIFACT_DIR}/nsys/${JOB_ID} \
  --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --cpuctx-sw-threads true --sample=none -- python -u tests/perf/run_trace_workload.py --model gpt-bert --seq 512 --batch 1
```
alex: We should also emit NVTX markers around kernel selection and KV cache ops so the timeline has semantic blocks.
josh: For kernel selection regressions we want to record: selected kernel name, sequence length, workspace size, and whether flash-attn/flashx or fallback implementation used. If we can't get the kernel name from the runtime, we can tag it with NVTX: `NVTX_PUSH("kernel_select:flash-attn")`.
maya: Storage plan: upload raw nsys (.qdrep/.qdpa) and a precomputed lightweight JSON summary with per-kernel aggregates to S3 under `s3://perf-artifacts/nightly/${JOB_ID}/`. Summary fields: model, seq_len, batch_size, quant, dominant_kernel, percent_time_dominant, kv_cache_miss_rate, token_p99_latency, artifact_url.
priya: What metrics do we diff in the dashboard to trigger alerts?
ajex: (typo) alex: Suggested regression rules:
- dominant_kernel change (string) for same model/seq/quant -> alert
- percent_time_dominant increase > 8% -> warn
- kv_cache_miss_rate delta > 5 percentage points -> alert
- token_p99_latency increase > 10% -> alert
We should also surface flamegraph diffs and a small timeline GIF for manual triage.
josh: On the trace processing side, we can run `nsys export --report=timeline` and then parse kernel timeline.csv to compute per-kernel time and counts. We should also capture CUDA memcpy and kernel launch overhead buckets.
maya: CI integration: add a workflow `perf-nightly-traces` that runs on a reserved GPU fleet, collects traces, uploads artifacts, and posts a short summary in #eng-runtime with links. Use the same artifact tags the rollout system uses so we can correlate with model pins.
priya: Can we avoid huge S3 costs? Maybe compress qdrep and keep only qdrep + small JSON; delete full capture after 30 days.
nsys-bot: [perf-nightly-traces/2201112222] Upload complete: 3 traces for gpt-bert/512/batch1/quant8 saved. Summary: dominant_kernel=flash-attn, percent_time=62%, kv_cache_miss_rate=3.1%, token_p99=41.2ms. Diff vs baseline: percent_time +12% (regression), token_p99 +9%. See: https://perf.redwood.example/summaries/2201112222
ci-collector-bot: Artifacts: https://s3.redwood.example/nightly/2201112222/nsys_1.qdrep (3.2GB), https://s3.redwood.example/nightly/2201112222/summary.json (2.4KB)
priya: The bot sees +12% percent_time for flash-attn — that's over the 8% threshold. Can we auto-create a ticket or flag the rollout page?
ajex: (typo) alex: Yes, pipeline should POST to our perf-regressions endpoint with the summary JSON; create a Jira with the key fields and attach the flamegraph diff. Triage flow: infra picks up, then runtime eng.
josh: Small follow-up — add a quick smoke run that forces KV cache cold/warm states so we can separate cache-induced regressions. NVTX markers: `NVTX_PUSH("kv_cache:miss")` and `NVTX_PUSH("kv_cache:hit")`.
maya: I'll draft a GH action / pipeline change and a small lambda that ingests the summary and updates the diff dashboard. Will post a PR in infra/perf later today.
alex: Awesome. If we can get this in next week we can catch the kernel-selection regression early before it rolls. :thumbsup:
priya: ack
maya: adding unit to infra backlog now.
nsys-bot: Logged regression ticket: PERF-4932 -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PERF-4932
ci-collector-bot: Upload retention policy: raw traces 30d, summaries 90d.
maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood/perf/pull/712 (WIP)
alex: thanks everyone, let's iterate on thresholds after first week of data.
priya: good plan.
